title: Road to bigger calves: 18 inches or bust!
summary: His 16-inch calves were built entirely by five years of football and basketball; he has never done a calf raise. In his garage gym without calf machines he plans three barbell-based calf movements with progressive loading to test whether small calves can grow, aiming for 18 inches.

claims.claim: He has never trained calves directly; five years of high-school football and college basketball (running, plyometrics) built them to 16 inches.
His calf goal is 18 inches, training in a garage gym without calf-raise or donkey-calf machines.
His plan uses three calf movements that only need a barbell and weights (plus a bench for one), including plain calf raises with an improvised machine.
He will add weight to these movements over time and check whether his calves grow as he gets stronger.
He challenges the common claim that calves are purely genetic and that small calves stay small forever, and sets out to test it.
With 26-inch thighs, his lower legs need to catch up after being neglected too long.

exercises.name: Improvised barbell calf raise
exercises.why: no calf machines in his garage gym
